# 1 Samuel Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 125r-125v | **Source Image:** 1SA_010_page_001.jpg, 1SA_010_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Then Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head and kissed him and said, "Has not the LORD anointed you as ruler over his inheritance?

**2** When you depart from me today, you will find two men by the tomb of Rachel in the territory of Benjamin at Zelzah, and they will say to you, 'The donkeys that you went to seek have been found. And behold, your father has abandoned the matter of the donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, "What shall I do about my son?"'

**3** And you shall pass on from there and beyond, and you shall come to the oak of Tabor, and three men going up to God at Bethel will find you there: one carrying three young goats, and one carrying three loaves of bread, and one carrying a skin of wine.

**4** And they will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, and you shall receive them from their hand.

**5** After that you will come to the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is. And it will be, when you come there to the city, that you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place, and before them a harp and a tambourine and a flute and a lyre, and they will be prophesying.

**6** And the spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be turned into another man.

**7** And it shall be, when these signs come upon you, do for yourself whatever your hand finds to do, for God is with you.

**8** And you shall go down before me to Gilgal, and behold, I am coming down to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you, and I will make known to you what you shall do."

**9** And it was so, when he turned his shoulder to depart from Samuel, that God gave him another heart, and all these signs came to pass on that day.

**10** And they came there to the hill, and behold, a band of prophets met him, and the spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.

**11** And it came to pass that all who knew him previously saw, and behold, he was prophesying with the prophets. And the people said to one another, "What is this that has come upon the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"

**12** And a man from there answered and said, "And who is their father?" Therefore it became a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

**13** And when he finished prophesying, he came to the high place.

**14** And the uncle of Saul said to him and to his servant, "Where did you go?" And he said, "To seek the donkeys, and when we saw that they were nowhere, we came to Samuel."

**15** And the uncle of Saul said, "Please tell me what Samuel said to you."

**16** And Saul said to his uncle, "He plainly told us that the donkeys had been found." But the matter of the kingship, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.

**17** And Samuel summoned the people to the LORD at Mizpah.

**18** And he said to the sons of Israel, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.'

**19** But you today have rejected your God, who himself saves you from all your calamities and your distresses, and you have said to him, 'No, but set a king over us.' Now therefore, present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your clans."

**20** And Samuel brought near all the tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken by lot.

**21** And he brought near the tribe of Benjamin by its clans, and the clan of the Matrites was taken, and Saul the son of Kish was taken. But when they sought him, he could not be found.

**22** And they inquired again of the LORD, "Has the man come here yet?" And the LORD said, "Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage."

**23** And they ran and took him from there, and he stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than any of the people from his shoulders and upward.

**24** And Samuel said to all the people, "Do you see him whom the LORD has chosen, that there is none like him among all the people?" And all the people shouted and said, "Long live the king!"

**25** And Samuel spoke to the people the manner of the kingship, and he wrote it in a scroll and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each man to his house.

**26** And Saul also went to his house at Gibeah, and the valiant men whose hearts God had touched went with him.

**27** But the sons of worthlessness said, "How can this one save us?" And they despised him and brought him no gift. But he was as one who was silent.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 1** — Heb. nagid: "ruler" (see note on 9:16). Samuel's act of anointing (mashach) with oil constitutes Saul as the LORD's mashiach ("anointed one"), a term that later acquires messianic significance.

**Verse 2** — "The tomb of Rachel" (qevurat Rachel): Located in Benjaminite territory according to this text (cf. Gen 35:19-20; Jer 31:15). The geographical note anchors the sign in a specific, verifiable location.

**Verse 5** — "The hill of God" (giv'at ha'elohim): Likely Gibeah of Saul, his home territory. The Philistine garrison there underscores Israel's subjugation and the urgency of the new leader's mission.

**Verse 6** — Heb. wetsalachah 'aleikha ruach YHWH: "And the spirit of the LORD will rush upon you." The verb tsalach connotes a sudden, powerful irruption — the same verb used of the spirit's action upon Samson (Judg 14:6).

**Verse 9** — Heb. lev 'acher: "another heart." God's transformation of Saul's inner disposition is immediate and supernatural, equipping him for the role of ruler.

**Verse 12** — "And who is their father?": An enigmatic retort. Prophecy is a gift of the spirit, not a matter of lineage. The question dismisses the crowd's surprise by asserting that prophetic calling transcends social origin.

**Verse 22** — Saul's hiding among the baggage (kelim) has been read as humility, reluctance, or fear. The narrative deliberately withholds Saul's motivation, allowing the reader to assess his character as events unfold.

**Verse 25** — "The manner of the kingship" (mishpat hammelukha): Distinct from the "manner of the king" in 8:11. This document establishes the constitutional limits of royal authority, written and deposited before the LORD as a covenantal witness.

**Verse 27** — Heb. benei beliyya'al: "sons of worthlessness." The term beliyya'al designates those who reject divine and social order. Their contempt for the LORD's chosen ruler foreshadows future division.

-- LOGOS
